toolInput.rationale:
Consolidation requires first establishing ground truth (current time, open CRM tickets, and full detail on each) before deciding which are true duplicates, since only tickets describing the same underlying incident may be merged. Severity and routing must then be derived strictly from the escalation matrix and on-call schedule at the survivor's SLA deadline, per policy, rather than assumed.</rationale>
<steps>
<steps>Call get_current_time to anchor all subsequent deadline/routing calculations.</steps>
<steps>Call list_tickets with status=new and status=open (and escalated, if any) filtered to service=crm to get the full set of open CRM tickets.</steps>
<steps>Call get_ticket on each open CRM ticket to read its description, impact scope, creation time, existing SLA deadline, and links, to determine which ones genuinely describe the same underlying incident (not just similar wording).</steps>
<steps>Call get_escalation_matrix for service=crm to find the correct severity for the confirmed incident's impact scope, and the response target/escalation rotation for that severity.</steps>
<steps>Identify the survivor as the earliest-created ticket among the confirmed duplicates; determine the correct SLA deadline for the survivor as the earliest deadline among the set (if none of the duplicates has a deadline yet, compute one as current time + response target for the assigned severity).</steps>
<steps>Call merge_tickets with survivorId set to the earliest-created duplicate, duplicateIds set to the rest of the confirmed-duplicate set, and slaDueAt set to the determined earliest deadline; leave any non-matching CRM tickets untouched.</steps>
<steps>Call set_severity on the survivor ticket using the value read from the escalation matrix for its service/impact scope.</steps>
<steps>Call get_oncall for the CRM rotation named in the escalation matrix, with `at` set to the survivor's SLA deadline, then call assign_ticket (or escalate_ticket if severity warrants escalation per the matrix) to that on-call engineer, and post_comment summarizing which tickets were merged and why.</steps>
</steps>
